newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Naphtha firms, gasoline steady.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas- Naphtha firms, gasoline steady.

text.p: Naphtha prices firmed, led mainly by strong overnight crude gains but cash fundamental was weak as seen by the poor Taiwan tender award, traders said on Thursday.
Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) has awarded its tender to buy August naphthenic and aromatic naphtha (N+A) at $193 per tonne.
The 28,000-tonne cargo was for August 1-10 delivery on a cost and freight basis to Kaohsiung.
This compares with CPC's last tender, for July 20-31 delivery which was awarded at slightly above $215 per tonne c+f Kaohsiung.
A CPC official said it will decide on Friday whether to buy a second cargo for second half August arrival.
Traders said the lower award were indicative that cash fundamental is weak.
They said prices are expected to move lower in the near term. FOB Singapore light naphtha were assessed at a premium of 45 cents to Singapore spot quotes, majors said.

On term Abu Dhabi naphtha, Asian term lifters have accepted ADNOC's offer prices of $21 a tonne premium over the ADNOC formula for a one-year supply contract, totalling 700,000 tonnes starting in July.
This is up from the previous premium of $6.80 per tonne.
The gasoline market was dead, traders said. Buyers and sellers were sidelined as most were speculating on potential Indonesian demand.
Indonesia is expected to import gasoline to fill the gap in supplies while two of its refineries undergo maintenance.
But fundamentals remained soft, as supplies were more than adequate to meet demand, traders said.
Traders dismissed trade development board stocks figures for light distillates which showed a marginal drop of 47,000 barrels to 6.05 million barrels.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
